exposure: Pre-pregnancy high-risk factors (age < 18 and ≥ 35 years, previous miscarriage, grand multiparity, diabetes in family, previous prematurity, overweight/obesity, previous cesarean section and previous pre-eclampsia)
Women who had infants with small for gestational age (SGA)
Women who delivered by cesarean section
outcome: Occurrence of Great Obstetrical Syndromes (GOS), including cesarean section, prematurity, SGA, and stillbirth
cohort: 412 women who delivered at the University Clinics of Kinshasa, DR Congo
finding: Maternal anemia was highly prevalent (53.4%) and significantly associated with increased risk of malaria, urinary infection, cesarean section, prematurity, SGA, and stillbirth, with pre-pregnancy high-risk factors further exacerbating these risks.
mod_finding: Maternal anemia was significantly linked to cesarean section.
